A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Quaffure and provide readable, matching sections, equations, figures, and tables across 11 pages each. Neither contains an appendix or embedded attachment. Both reference separate supplementary material that is absent from the supplied files.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original hair-simulation experiments, quantitative baseline comparisons in Table 1, runtime measurements, and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports gravity-potential values and a qualitative comparison of two potential formulations.

M1.justification: Section 3.5 adds an optional shear-only potential using current segment length instead of rest length for normalization. The original formulation and network architecture remain; the PDFs do not establish that this option replaced the loss used for the existing experiments.

E1.justification: Both use CT-groom data supplemented by artist-created grooms and retain the same hairstyle, body-shape, pose, and temporal evaluations. The new extreme-pose caveat does not document additional evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Adam, L-BFGS, XPBD (GPU), and GroomGen. The mass-spring comparator in Figure 10 is also retained.

E3.justification: Table 1 adds gravity potential as a reference evaluation quantity alongside the existing metrics. Retained experimental settings, including GroomGen's 1000 sampled poses and XPBD's 10000 iterations and 30 time steps, are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 3.5 newly reports that the original and shear-only potentials produced similar results, providing a brief qualitative comparison without a dedicated quantitative ablation. The mass-spring and stiffness ablations in Figures 10–11 remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added gravity-potential values follow the existing point-value reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds gravity potentials: Adam 3011.33, L-BFGS 3047.53, XPBD 3507.53, GroomGen 3889.78, and Quaffure 3399.95. All existing timing, intersection, length-preservation, and orientation-preservation values remain unchanged. Section 3.5 also adds the finding of similar results for both potential variants.

T1.justification: After Equation 7, v2 introduces a distinct strain definition normalized by current segment length, removing the stretching contribution from that potential. The remaining mathematics is retained apart from renaming the modified stretch-shear potential as the Cosserat potential; no proof is added.

C1.justification: The introduction and final contribution bullet shift from generalizing across hairstyles, poses, and shapes to modeling different hairstyles while generalizing across poses and shapes. Table 1 similarly drops groom generalization. The abstract retains its broader wording, and the central self-supervision and real-time claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 newly acknowledges implausible deformations for physically infeasible poses absent from training, exemplified by excessive backward neck bending. Section 4.2 narrows the assertion of no instabilities to no time-integration instabilities.

D1.justification: Section 4.4 removes the explicit statement that stiffness parameters are varied during training, slightly reducing the specificity of the ablation documentation. Representation dimensions, PyTorch implementation, hardware, baseline implementation details, and supplementary-material access statements are retained.

R1.justification: Table 1 narrows the advertised generalization advantage relative to GroomGen by omitting grooms. The remark about Hsu et al. achieving upsampling from 128 guide strands is removed, although that work remains cited. The same 52 references and main related-work discussion are retained.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted wording corrections and condenses the XPBD, performance, ablation, and limitations passages. It also renames the modified potential. Section ordering and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a gravity-potential column, smaller text, and a revised caption. Figure 1's raster dimensions are approximately halved. Experimental image panels remain identical, with local text and figure reflow; the conclusion now fits on page 8.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves scientific precision by narrowing hairstyle-generalization claims and acknowledging extreme-pose failures. Gravity diagnostics and the explicit alternative potential add useful transparency. These gains outweigh the small loss of training-time stiffness-ablation wording, while the unchanged principal experiments and still-broad abstract limit the overall improvement.
